source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. The final battle, first form: the Hollow King, a vast shadow of swirling blank white pages that would erase every story ever told. Solemn, majestic and grand, like a requiem sung in a cathedral at the end of the world; awe and holy dread rather than speed. A slow, noble chorale melody carried by organ, choir and brass over a steady, inexorable battle pulse that never stops. Tempo 120 BPM, 4/4 time, key of D minor. Instrumentation: grand pipe organ, a large wordless choir (no words), low brass chorale of trombones and tuba, tolling cathedral bells, timpani, deep taiko-like drums, a steady low string ostinato, harp. Form: organ and tolling bell intro; section A grand choir and brass chorale over the low string ostinato and drums; section B a darker, quieter organ passage with the pulse still beating; section A returns fuller with timpani and bells; the last bar leads back to section A. Duration: 120 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
